title: My grandfather's map
goal: Say whatever happens and wherever you go, and read a story of wishes and regrets.

intro.text: Repeat the verb after a question word with `-sA`, and it means **no matter**: *Ne olursa olsun* (whatever happens), *Kim gelirse gelsin* (whoever comes). This lesson mixes every form of the unit around an old sea map.

vocab.en: direction, way (yönümüzü kaybettik: we lost our way)

exercises.title: Dedemin haritası
exercises.passage:
Geçen yaz dedemin eski evini toplarken bir dolabın içinde büyük, sararmış bir harita buldum. Haritada okyanuslar, adalar ve kıyılar vardı; kenarlarında da dedemin el yazısıyla küçük notlar.

Haritayı dedeme gösterdim. Önce uzun uzun baktı, sonra güldü: “Bu harita benim hayalimdi. Gençken denizci olmak istiyordum. Param olsaydı bir tekne alırdım, bütün kıyıları dolaşırdım. Ama babam istemedi, ben de vazgeçtim.”

“Keşke vazgeçmeseydin.” dedim.

“Bazen ben de öyle düşünüyorum. Gitseydim belki hiç dönmezdim, belki de büyük bir kaptan olurdum. Kim bilir? Ama gitseydim sen bu evde büyümezdin, belki hiç doğmazdın.”

Sonra haritayı bana verdi: “Ne olursa olsun, hayallerinden vazgeçme. Nereye gidersen git, bu harita seninle olsun. Yönünü kaybetsen bile yolunu bulursun.”

Şimdi harita odamın duvarında asılı. Keşke dedem şimdi genç olsa; birlikte giderdik. Ama ne yaparsam yapayım, zamanı geri getiremem. Bu yüzden bu yaz ilk kez tek başıma bir tekne yolculuğuna çıkacağım.

glossary.en: for a long time, at length

exercises.translation: Last summer, while I was tidying my grandfather's old house, I found a big, yellowed map inside a cupboard. On the map there were oceans, islands and coasts, and in the margins small notes in my grandfather's handwriting. I showed the map to my grandfather. First he looked at it for a long time, then he laughed: “This map was my dream. When I was young, I wanted to be a sailor. If I'd had the money, I would have bought a boat and sailed along every coast. But my father didn't want it, and I gave up.” “I wish you hadn't given up,” I said. “Sometimes I think so too. If I had gone, maybe I would never have come back, or maybe I would have become a great captain. Who knows? But if I had gone, you wouldn't have grown up in this house; maybe you would never have been born.” Then he gave me the map: “Whatever happens, don't give up on your dreams. Wherever you go, let this map be with you. Even if you lose your way, you'll find your path.” Now the map hangs on the wall of my room. I wish my grandfather were young now; we would go together. But whatever I do, I can't bring back time. So this summer, for the first time, I'm going on a boat trip on my own.

questions.q: Why didn't the grandfather become a sailor?
options: His father didn't want him to
He didn't have a boat
He was afraid of the sea
questions.explain: *Babam istemedi, ben de vazgeçtim.* The money comes in only as an unreal past: *Param olsaydı…*

questions.q: *Gitseydim belki hiç dönmezdim.* What does the grandfather mean?
options: If he had gone, he might never have come back
He went and never came back
He will go and won't come back
questions.explain: `-sAydI` and `-mAzdI`: a past that didn't happen, and what would have followed.

questions.q: What does he tell his grandchild?
options: Never give up on your dreams, whatever happens
Stay at home and be careful
Sell the map one day

questions.q: What does the writer decide to do?
options: Go on a boat trip alone this summer
Become a captain
Give the map back
questions.explain: *Bu yaz ilk kez tek başıma bir tekne yolculuğuna çıkacağım.*

reject.why: The second *olmak* isn't the aorist: it repeats the verb as **let it be**, *olsun*.
The second verb isn't another condition: it's the third-person imperative, *olsun*.

exercises.hint: The same verb again, as **let it be**.
exercises.explain: *Ne olursa olsun*: question word + `-(I)rsA` + the same verb in `-sIn`.

exercises.label: **Whatever I do, whatever you do…**: type both verbs that follow *ne*
exercises.explain: The first verb is the aorist conditional; the second is each person's optative or imperative: *yapayım, yap, yapsın, yapalım, yapın, yapsınlar*.

exercises.prompt: Whoever comes, don't open the door.
exercises.explain: *Kim gelirse gelsin*: **whoever comes**, the same verb repeated in `-sIn`.

accept: Whatever he says, do not believe him.
No matter what he says, do not believe him.
[Whatever|No matter what] she says, do not believe her.
Do not believe him, [whatever|no matter what] he says.
Do not believe her, [whatever|no matter what] she says.

exercises.question: *Nereye gidersen git, seni bulurum.* What does it mean?
options: Wherever you go, I'll find you.
If you go, I'll find you.
Where are you going? I'll find you.

why.1: That would be *Gidersen seni bulurum*, without the question word and the repeated verb.
why.2: There's no question: *nereye … git* means **wherever you go**.

exercises.explain: Question word + `-(I)rsA` + the same verb in the imperative: **no matter where**.

exercises.en: Whatever happens, don't give up on your dreams.

exercises.text: If we had had a compass, we would not have lost our way.
accept: We would not have lost our way if we had had a compass.

exercises.prompt: Even if I were rich, I wouldn't buy that car.
accept: Zengin olsam bile o arabayı almazdım.
Zengin olsam da o arabayı almazdım.

reject.why: *Zenginsem* is a real condition, **if I'm rich**. For **if I were**, go through *olmak*: *zengin olsam*.

exercises.explain: *Zengin olsam bile*: even if I were rich. *Almazdım*: I wouldn't buy.

exercises.question: Fill in: *Dün akşam vaktim ___ sana gelirdim.*
options: olsaydı
varsa
olursa

why.1: *Varsa* is a real condition about now, and *dün akşam* is in the past.

exercises.explain: A past that didn't happen: *vaktim olsaydı … gelirdim*.

exercises.task: Imagine you could live in any century and any place. In three or four sentences, say where you would live, what you would do and what you would miss. Use `-sA` … `-(I)rdI`, and *keşke* at least once.
models: 16. yüzyılda yaşasam İstanbul'da bir gemide çalışırdım. Kaptan olsam bütün Akdeniz'i dolaşırdım. Telefonum olmazdı, ama yeni yerler keşfederdim. Keşke o zamanın haritalarını görebilsem.
Yüz yıl önce yaşasam bir köyde otururdum. Her sabah erken kalkardım ve bahçede çalışırdım. Arkadaşlarıma mektup yazardım. Ama internet olmasa çok sıkılırdım; keşke ikisi birden olsa.

exercises.tr: Kim ne derse desin, ben gidiyorum.
options: Kim ne derse desin, ben gidiyorum.
Kim ne dedi? Ben gidiyorum.
Kim gelirse gelsin, ben gidiyorum.

exercises.question: Can really wants to go. What does he answer?

context.en: Shall we go to the sea tomorrow?
They say the weather will be bad tomorrow.

options: Olsun, hava kötü olsa bile gidelim.
Keşke hava kötü olsaydı.
Hava kötü olursa gitmeyelim.

why.1: *Keşke … olsaydı* wishes the weather had been bad: the opposite of what Can wants.
why.2: That gives up: **if the weather is bad, let's not go**.

exercises.explain: *Olsun* (never mind) and *-sA bile* (even if): Can wants to go anyway.
